Motorcycle Breakdown Cover for Touring

Breakdown cover might be the best £60-120 you spend on your entire tour. When your bike stops on a Highland single-track road with no phone signal and 40 miles to the nearest garage, having someone to call changes everything. Here's how to choose the right cover.

RAC vs AA: The Big Two Compared

Both the RAC and AA offer motorcycle-specific breakdown cover with similar structures:

RAC Motorcycle Breakdown

  • Roadside assistance: Included at all levels. A patrol will attempt to fix your bike at the roadside.
  • Recovery: If roadside repair isn't possible, they'll transport you and your bike to a garage or your home.
  • At Home: Available on higher tiers. Covers breakdowns at your home address — useful for departure-day disasters.
  • Onward travel: Top-tier cover includes alternative transport, accommodation, or hire vehicle if your bike needs overnight repair.
  • App: The RAC app allows GPS-located breakdown requests — very useful when you can't describe exactly where you are on a rural road.

AA Motorcycle Breakdown

  • Roadside assistance: Core cover at all levels with 24/7 response.
  • Recovery: Included from the second tier upwards. They'll take you and your bike to a destination of your choice within the UK.
  • At Home: Added from the Homestart level — essential for touring.
  • Onward travel: Top-tier benefit covering overnight accommodation, car hire, or taxi to your next destination.
  • Motorcycle-specific patrols: The AA has trained motorcycle technicians in some regions who carry common bike-specific tools and parts.
For touring specifically, we recommend the second-highest tier from either provider as a minimum. You need roadside, recovery, and home-start as absolute essentials. Onward travel is a valuable bonus for multi-day tours.

Response Times in Remote Areas

In built-up areas, both services typically respond within 30-60 minutes. In remote Scotland, Wales, or northern England, response times can stretch to 2-4 hours. This is a reality of the geography, not a failure of the service.

  • In areas with no phone signal, you may need to walk or ride to get a signal before calling. Save the breakdown number offline.
  • Some services allow you to text your location if signal is poor.
  • Consider carrying a personal locator beacon (PLB) for truly remote touring — it's a safety device, not a breakdown tool, but it's an extra layer.

Specialist Motorcycle Breakdown Providers

Beyond the RAC and AA, specialist options include:

  • National Motorcyclists Council (NMC) rescue: Specifically designed for motorcyclists with motorcycle-trained recovery drivers.
  • Bennetts Motorcycle Rescue: Available as part of Bennetts insurance, with motorcycle-specific expertise.
  • GEM Motoring Assist: A smaller provider with good motorcycle cover and competitive prices.

What Breakdown Cover Doesn't Cover

Important limitations to understand:

  • Running out of fuel (some providers charge for fuel delivery; others don't cover it)
  • Pre-existing known faults (if your bike had a problem before departure, it's not covered)
  • Off-road breakdowns (most policies only cover public roads)
  • Keys locked in or lost (some cover this, many don't — check)

Touring-Specific Tips

  • Download the provider's app and test it before departure
  • Save the breakdown phone number in your phone contacts AND written on a card in your wallet
  • Know your policy number by heart or have it easily accessible
  • Take a photo of your membership card
  • Brief your riding group on the procedure if someone breaks down

Breakdown cover is touring peace of mind. The cost is negligible compared to a single recovery without it — and on a motorcycle tour, it lets you push into the remote, beautiful corners of Britain knowing you've got a safety net.

You need roadside, recovery and home-start as essentials, with onward travel a valuable bonus.

faq.q: Which tier of breakdown cover do I need for touring?
faq.a: For touring specifically, take the second-highest tier from either provider as a minimum. You need roadside assistance, recovery and home-start as absolute essentials, and onward travel, which provides a taxi, accommodation or hire vehicle if your bike needs overnight repair, is a valuable bonus on multi-day tours.

faq.q: How do RAC and AA compare?
faq.a: Both offer motorcycle-specific cover with similar structures. RAC includes roadside at all levels, recovery when roadside repair fails, and a GPS-located breakdown request in its app. The AA offers 24/7 roadside at all levels, recovery from the second tier, home-start from the Homestart level, and motorcycle-trained patrols in some regions.

faq.q: How long will help take in remote areas?
faq.a: In built-up areas both services typically respond within 30 to 60 minutes, but in remote Scotland, Wales or northern England response times can stretch to 2 to 4 hours. This is the reality of the geography rather than a failure of the service, so save the breakdown number offline and consider a personal locator beacon for very remote touring.

faq.q: What does breakdown cover not include?
faq.a: Common exclusions are running out of fuel (some providers charge for delivery, others do not cover it), pre-existing known faults, off-road breakdowns since most policies only cover public roads, and keys locked in or lost, which some cover but many do not. Check each of these before you rely on your policy.

faq.q: How should I prepare for a possible breakdown?
faq.a: Download the provider's app and test it before departure, save the breakdown number in your phone contacts and written on a card in your wallet, know your policy number or keep it easily accessible, photograph your membership card, and brief your riding group on the procedure so everyone knows what to do if someone breaks down.
